note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`. FIXED 2026-09-06 (was a VERIFIED ENGINE GAP): the three personas below with names ending '-now-correctly-critical' used to document a genuine safety-relevant discordance — hasToxicResult() and classifyResult()/gradeFollowUp()'s critical-escalation checks only recognised paracetamol-above-the-line or the toxicLevelPresent/overallResultStatus='critical' booleans, so a numerically toxic lithium, carboxyhaemoglobin, or salicylate level on its own did NOT auto-escalate Axis A/D or raise F-CRITICAL-RESULT-001, even though it did drive severity to 'major' via the separate over-toxic-threshold rule (R-SEV-MAJOR-02); the salicylate case was the worst of the three, since F-URGENT-REFERRAL-001's own condition additionally omitted salicylate, leaving it completely unflagged. Fixed by adding the same three over-threshold conditions to a new `isCriticalResult()` predicate (deliberately not folded into hasToxicResult() itself, which gradeSeverity checks first — that would have made its own dedicated R-SEV-MAJOR-02 branch unreachable dead code) and to F-URGENT-REFERRAL-001's condition; classifyResult(), F-CRITICAL-RESULT-001, F-ABNORMAL-ACTION-001's exclusion, and F-UNEXPECTED-FINDING-001 all now call isCriticalResult() instead of duplicating the old, narrower condition inline.

personas.name: lithium-severely-toxic-now-correctly-critical
personas.description: FIXED 2026-09-06 (was 'lithium-severely-toxic-not-critical-classification-gap', a real, verified engine gap): a severely toxic lithium level (3.2 mmol/L, more than double the 1.5 mmol/L threshold) with neither toxicLevelPresent nor overallResultStatus ticked used to leave resultClassification 'normal' and followUpUrgency only 'urgent' (not 'critical-alert'), even though abnormalitySeverity correctly graded 'major' via R-SEV-MAJOR-02 — classifyResult() and gradeFollowUp() only checked hasToxicResult(), not the separate over-toxic-threshold check gradeSeverity() already used. Fixed by adding the same three over-threshold conditions to isCriticalResult() (deliberately not folded into hasToxicResult() itself, which would have made R-SEV-MAJOR-02 unreachable dead code). Now correctly resultClassification 'critical', followUpUrgency 'critical-alert', with F-CRITICAL-RESULT-001/002 firing alongside F-URGENT-REFERRAL-001.

personas.name: salicylate-toxic-now-correctly-critical
personas.description: FIXED 2026-09-06 (was 'salicylate-toxic-completely-unflagged-classification-gap', the most severe instance of this engine gap: unlike the lithium/carboxyhaemoglobin personas, F-URGENT-REFERRAL-001's own hand-rolled condition previously omitted salicylate entirely, so a toxic salicylate level had no safety net of any kind): a toxic salicylate level (>=300 mg/L) with neither toxicLevelPresent nor overallResultStatus ticked used to leave resultClassification 'normal', followUpUrgency only 'urgent', AND raised no flag at all — completely invisible to a clinician scanning fired rules and flags, despite abnormalitySeverity correctly grading 'major' via R-SEV-MAJOR-02. Fixed by adding the over-threshold check to isCriticalResult() and adding salicylate to F-URGENT-REFERRAL-001's own condition (it already imported the SALICYLATE_TOXIC_MG_L constant for gradeSeverity's use). Now correctly resultClassification 'critical', followUpUrgency 'critical-alert', with F-CRITICAL-RESULT-001/002 firing alongside F-URGENT-REFERRAL-001.

personas.name: paracetamol-below-treatment-line-minor-severity-falls-to-routine
personas.description: Paracetamol level plotted below the MHRA nomogram treatment line, a reassuring result — classification 'normal' (the same as a completely blank study) but abnormalitySeverity resolves to 'minor' rather than 'none' (R-SEV-MINOR-01), a distinct 'normal but minor' pairing from the lithium/carboxyhaemoglobin/salicylate gap personas above (which were 'normal but major'). A second real, verified engine characteristic: gradeFollowUp() has no explicit branch for severity 'minor' at all (unlike every sibling test-result engine authored earlier this session, which all had an explicit minor -> 'recommended, per local pathway' branch) — it simply falls through to the routine default (R-FU-ROUTINE-01), so this reassuring-but-not-blank result gets exactly the same follow-up urgency as a fully normal study.
